The handling for directory crc hash overflows was fairly obscure
split_leaf returns EOVERFLOW when we try to extend the item and that is
supposed to bubble up to userland.  For a while it did so
way we added better handling of errors and forced the FS readonly if we
hit IO errors during the directory insertion.
Along the way
column2: we started testing only for EEXIST and the EOVERFLOW case

column1: was dropped.  The end result is that we may force the FS readonly if we
catch a directory hash bucket overflow.
This fixes a few problem spots.  First I add tests for EOVERFLOW in the
places where we can safely just return the error up the chain.
btrfs_rename is harder though
column2: because it tries to insert the new

column1: directory item only after it has already unlinked anything the rename
was going to overwrite.  Rather than adding very complex logic
a helper to test for the hash overflow case early while it is still safe
to bail out.
Snapshot and subvolume creation had a similar problem
the new helper now too.
